record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is it decidable whether p is k-avoidable, given a pattern p and an integer k?

evidence.quote: Is it decidable whether p is k-avoidable, given a pattern p and an integer k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet of letters and let E = {x_1, x_2, ...} be a disjoint countable set of variables. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E^+. A word w ∈ A^* is said to encounter the pattern p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : E^+ → A^+ such that h(p) is a factor (contiguous subword) of w; otherwise w avoids p. For a positive integer k, the pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over an alphabet of size k that avoids p (equivalently, infinitely many finite words over a k-letter alphabet avoid p), and p is k-unavoidable otherwise.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input an arbitrary pattern p ∈ E^+ and a positive integer k, decides whether p is k-avoidable?
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability of k-avoidability of a pattern (equivalently, computability of the avoidability index μ(p)) is widely cited as an open problem in combinatorics on words. Surveys and tutorials note no known algorithm computes μ(p), and even specific small patterns (e.g. ααββγγ) have unknown avoidability index, indicating the general decision problem remains unresolved as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorics on Words – A Tutorial (Berstel, Karhumäki)
status_evidence.snippet: No known algorithm to compute the avoidability index of a given pattern; even μ(ααββγγ) is not known to be 2 or 3.
status_evidence.claim: The decidability of computing the avoidability index of a pattern is open.

status_evidence.title: Outstanding Challenges in Combinatorics on Words (BIRS 12w5068)
status_evidence.snippet: Workshop report listing pattern avoidance decidability among outstanding challenges.
status_evidence.claim: k-avoidability decidability is listed among open challenges in combinatorics on words.
